scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. My son woke up and he was surprised when he saw me. He told me that I should’ve called him or something. We talked for a bit and he seemed kinda annoyed. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

prediction.raw: I would say 1, YTA (You're The Asshole). Here's why: Visiting your son unannounced, especially when he's made it clear that he needs space, can be seen as overstepping and disrespecting his boundaries. As a 19-year-old university student, he's likely trying to establish his independence and navigate his new life away from home. By showing up unannounced, you may have caught him off guard and made him feel uncomfortable or even embarrassed, especially if he was sleeping or in the middle of something. His reaction, although seemingly annoyed, is understandable given the circumstances. It's also important to consider that your son has been trying to communicate his needs to you, albeit indirectly, by not answering your calls or hanging up. Instead of respecting his boundaries, you chose to visit him unannounced, which may have been perceived as dismissive of his needs. Additionally, your comment about the apartment needing a good clean, although likely made in jest, may have come across as judgmental or critical, which could have added to your son's annoyance. It's essential to respect your son's autonomy and boundaries, especially as he's transitioning into adulthood. Giving him space when he needs it and communicating openly and respectfully can help strengthen your relationship and build trust. In the future, it might be helpful to have an open and honest conversation with your son about your concerns and boundaries, and to establish a mutually respectful and considerate approach to communication and visits.
